Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 37 (Sabey Data Centers WA missing-address campaign): added a campus-confirmed shared address, refreshed and expanded company history and current national footprint from a fresh Wikipedia check, campus-total capacity context. research_status remains complete.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Sabey Corporation was founded in 1972 by Dave Sabey as a Pacific Northwest commercial real estate developer. Sabey Data Centers own site describes the data center business beginning almost by accident, during the dot com collapse a tenant vacated a Sabey owned building, leaving an abandoned data center facility that became SDC Seattle, building 5, and prompted the company pivot into the data center industry, Sabey Data Center Properties operates as a joint venture between Sabey Corporation and investor National Real Estate Advisors, per both the operators own site and this sessions fresh Wikipedia check, which corroborates the joint venture structure. A prior research pass on these rows recorded the company as operating six data center campuses nationally encompassing more than 3.5 million square feet. This sessions fresh Wikipedia check finds the company has grown since that prior figure was recorded, current Wikipedia coverage describes more than 3.5 million square feet and nearly 400 megawatts of capacity across a wider footprint, Seattle, Washington, Quincy and East Wenatchee, Washington (Columbia River region campuses powered by hydroelectricity), Ashburn, Virginia (a third building under construction, roughly 85 MW total campus capacity planned), Manhattan, New York (Intergate Manhattan at 375 Pearl Street, retrofitted from a former Verizon/NY Telephone building, opened 2013), the Austin, Texas metro area in Round Rock (first building completed October 2024, 430,000 square feet, 84 MW critical power), and Umatilla, Oregon (a planned 100 plus MW campus in development). Leadership also changed recently, Tim Mirick became president effective January 1, 2025, succeeding Rob Rockwood, per this sessions Wikipedia check. This registry tracks 11 Sabey rows across two Washington state campuses only, SDC Seattle in Tukwila/King County and SDC Columbia in East Wenatchee/Douglas County, the Virginia, New York, Texas, and Oregon locations described above are not tracked as rows in this registry. Per the operators own current SDC Seattle page, that Tukwila campus totals over a million square feet and 54 MW of capacity campus wide, a figure not broken out per building, so not applied to critical_it_mw for any individual row. Per the operators own current SDC Columbia page, that East Wenatchee campus is at 4405 Grant Rd, East Wenatchee, WA 98802, marketed on renewable hydroelectric power at 5 cents per kWh, with three buildings on campus and a fourth under construction, totaling 70 MW of capacity campus wide, also not broken out per building and not applied to critical_it_mw for any individual row. An aggregator, Baxtel, separately notes 9 MW of additional Tier III standard critical power expected available at SDC Columbia from Q4 2026, a forward looking, not yet delivered figure as of this research session, recorded as planned capacity rather than applied to critical_it_mw. This specific row, Intergate Columbia A, is one of the buildings on the SDC Columbia campus. This registry has not found a distinct, separate street number for Building A specifically, unlike Buildings B and D which aggregator datacenterHawk lists individually, so the shared campus address from the operators own page is applied here instead, consistent with a shared campus address pattern seen at several other multi-building campuses in this registry.
